checks.prompt: Instruction: ONE WORD FROM THE TEXT. Text: “Visitors leave valuables in lockers.” Which answer completes “Valuables are stored in ___”?
options: lockers
secure cupboards
in lockers
checks.explanation: Lockers procede del texto, encaja y respeta una palabra; el sinónimo no cumple la instrucción.

retrieval.prompt: Text: “Staff leave completed forms in a tray. The coordinator checks the signatures, then scans the forms. Paper copies go into a cabinet after scanning. Incomplete forms are returned to applicants.” Complete with ONE WORD from the text: 1: Signatures checked by the ___. 2: Paper forms stored in a ___ after scanning. 3: Incomplete forms sent back to ___. Give each answer and quote its evidence.
retrieval.explanation: Relee los resultados completos y distingue etapas; el orden de las notas no sustituye la comprobación.
retrieval.model: 1 coordinator: “The coordinator checks the signatures”. 2 cabinet: “Paper copies go into a cabinet after scanning”. 3 applicants: incomplete forms “are returned to applicants”. Tray is an earlier holding place, not the final storage location after scanning.
checklist: Uso palabras exactas del texto.
Distingo actor, lugar y destinatario.
Respeto una palabra y justifico cada hueco.

sources.title: IELTS: Reading General Training, formato y habilidades

why: Un esquema aporta un punto de vista que debes mantener estable. Derecha e izquierda pueden depender de hacia dónde miras, mientras norte y sur siguen una orientación fija. Conecta cada etiqueta con su referencia explícita antes de responder. En preguntas cortas, conserva además la categoría solicitada: lugar, objeto o persona. No conviertas una ubicación cercana en la parte realmente señalada.

decisions.cue: El plano fija el norte arriba y la entrada al sur.
decisions.action: Convierte las direcciones en posiciones del plano.
decisions.en: Walking north from the entrance, the workshop is on your left: west.
decisions.reason: La izquierda de quien mira al norte corresponde al oeste.

decisions.cue: La pregunta pide dónde se guarda un objeto dentro de una sala.
decisions.action: Sigue la segunda relación y nombra el contenedor.
decisions.en: The keys are in a cupboard inside the workshop.
decisions.reason: Workshop ubica la sala; cupboard responde al almacenamiento específico.

worked.scenario: The arts centre entrance is on the south side of the building. Visitors walk north from the entrance to reception. From there, the workshop is on the left and the office is on the right. The archive is directly beyond reception, further north; it can be entered only with a staff member. Spare keys are kept in a cupboard inside the workshop, not at the reception desk. A notice outside the office gives telephone numbers for course enquiries. All these rooms are on the ground floor, so visitors following this route do not need to use the stairs.
worked.task: Plan: NORTH at top. North of reception: [B]. West of reception: [A]. East: office. South: entrance. Complete A and B with ONE WORD from the text. Then answer with ONE WORD: Where inside the workshop are spare keys kept? Justify each answer.
worked.model: A: workshop. B: archive. Short answer: cupboard. From the south entrance a visitor faces north, so left maps to west. Beyond reception is further north. The final question asks for the container inside the room, not the room itself.

reasoning.quote: the workshop is on the left
reasoning.explanation: Al caminar hacia el norte, la izquierda corresponde al oeste del plano.

reasoning.quote: The archive is directly beyond reception, further north
reasoning.explanation: Dos referencias coincidentes sitúan archive al norte.

reasoning.quote: Spare keys are kept in a cupboard inside the workshop
reasoning.explanation: La pregunta interior requiere cupboard, aunque workshop también sea una ubicación verdadera.

alternative.text: A: office; short answer: workshop.
alternative.why: Office está a la derecha, es decir, al este desde la orientación dada. Workshop identifica la sala, pero la pregunta pide el lugar dentro de ella: cupboard.

checks.prompt: A plan has north at the top. You face north at reception. Why does a room on your left appear west of reception?
options: Left and west match from that stated viewpoint.
Left always means east on every plan.
Reception changes the direction of north.
checks.explanation: La correspondencia depende de la orientación explícita.

checks.prompt: Text: “The pump is below the tank.” Diagram from top to bottom: [tank] / [___]. Write ONE WORD from the text.
checks.explanation: Below sitúa pump en la posición inferior.

checks.prompt: Text: “The spare batteries are in a drawer inside the office.” Question: “Where inside the office are the batteries kept?” ONE WORD.
options: office
drawer
batteries
checks.explanation: Inside the office ya fija la sala; falta el contenedor solicitado.

retrieval.prompt: Text: “Enter the gallery from the west and walk east to the information desk. Facing east, the studio is on your right. The café is on your left. Spare brushes are in a cabinet inside the studio.” With north at the top, identify which room is south of the desk and where the spare brushes are kept. Give the two answers and explain the orientation using evidence.
retrieval.explanation: No reutilices automáticamente izquierda=oeste: ahora el visitante mira al este.
retrieval.model: The studio is south of the desk: visitors face east, and the studio is “on your right”, which points south from that viewpoint. The brushes are in a cabinet, supported by “in a cabinet inside the studio”. Studio answers the room-position question; cabinet answers the storage question.
checklist: Mantengo la orientación hacia el este.
Distingo sala y contenedor.
Doy respuestas y evidencia para ambas relaciones.

sources.title: IELTS: Reading General Training, formato y habilidades

why: Una revisión eficaz localiza primero qué respuestas pueden corregirse con evidencia disponible y qué dudas necesitan otra lectura. Evita gastar todo el margen en una comparación incierta mientras quedan casillas vacías o errores claros de formato. El orden de revisión debe adaptarse a tus intentos registrados. Separa el dato correcto de su presentación: puedes comprenderlo y todavía escribir una respuesta inválida.

decisions.cue: Ya tienes evidencia y la respuesta excede el límite.
decisions.action: Reduce la respuesta sin perder el dato solicitado.
decisions.en: Applications close on 17 September. Closing date: 17 September.
decisions.reason: La preposición está fuera del dato necesario y cuenta como palabra si la escribes.

decisions.cue: Una pregunta sigue sin evidencia tras releer la zona relevante.
decisions.action: Marca una respuesta provisional y distribuye el tiempo restante.
decisions.en: Return to uncertain items after completing the remaining questions.
decisions.reason: Es una estrategia adaptable de práctica; no demuestra que la respuesta provisional sea correcta.

worked.scenario: The skills centre is accepting applications for its autumn workshop. Forms must arrive by 17 September; the course begins on 2 October. Participants should collect a confirmation email before attending. Gloves are provided, but everyone must bring suitable shoes. No registration fee is charged. On arrival, participants must show a photograph that matches the name on their application; a home address is not requested at the door. Anyone unable to attend should email reception as soon as possible so that the place can be offered to someone on the waiting list. The centre cannot accept visitors who have not registered.
worked.task: Review these answers. 1: Closing date? NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER. Student: “2 October”. 2: What equipment is provided? ONE WORD FROM THE TEXT. Student: “protective gloves”. 3: What must participants show on arrival? Choose ONE letter: A registration fee; B photograph; C home address. Student: “photograph”. Write the corrected answers and classify each error.
worked.model: 1: 17 September — the original confused the course start with the application deadline. 2: gloves — two words exceed ONE WORD, and protective was added. 3: B — the content was understood, but the instruction requires a letter.

reasoning.explanation: El plazo es 17 September; 2 October corresponde al inicio del curso. Se necesita comprobar la función de cada fecha.
Gloves procede del texto y tiene una palabra; protective añade contenido.
Esta instrucción exige B aunque photograph identifique correctamente el objeto.

alternative.text: 1: 2 October; 2: protective gloves; 3: photograph.
alternative.why: La primera confunde inicio y cierre. La segunda incumple el límite y añade una palabra ausente. La tercera no utiliza el código solicitado.

checks.prompt: Why should a review separate comprehension errors from formatting errors?
options: They call for different fixes and different follow-up practice.
Formatting is always more important than meaning.
A correct meaning guarantees a valid answer.
checks.explanation: Una confusión de fecha necesita releer relaciones; un código equivocado necesita ejecutar la consigna.

checks.prompt: Instruction: ONE WORD FROM THE TEXT. Text: “Visitors receive badges.” Student: “visitor badges”. Correct the answer.
checks.explanation: Badges es la palabra del texto; visitor excede el límite y modifica el dato.

checks.prompt: You have three minutes left, one blank item and two answers with clear word-limit errors. What is a reasonable review decision?
options: Spend all three minutes rereading one uncertain paragraph.
Correct the known format errors, attempt the blank item, then revisit the remaining uncertainty.
Delete every uncertain answer.
checks.explanation: Prioriza correcciones sustentadas y casillas pendientes; ajusta después a la dificultad y el tiempo real.

retrieval.prompt: Text: “The walking tour starts on 6 November. Bookings close on 1 November. Visitors receive maps at the entrance. No food is provided.” Review: 1 Closing date? NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER: “6 November”. 2 What is given out? ONE WORD: “printed maps”. Give corrected answers with evidence, classify the two errors and state which concrete check would prevent each.
retrieval.explanation: Primero responde y justifica; después usa la causa del error para proponer una revisión específica.
retrieval.model: 1: 1 November, supported by “Bookings close on 1 November”. This is a comprehension error: the original answer confuses start and deadline. Check the role of each date. 2: maps, supported by “Visitors receive maps”. This is a format and added-word error: check ONE WORD and copy only the text word.
checklist: Corrijo ambas respuestas con evidencia.
Distingo fecha equivocada y formato.
Propongo una comprobación concreta para cada causa.

sources.title: IELTS: Reading General Training, formato y habilidades
